description: Spacecraft communications subsystem (uplink/downlink/RF) fault knowledge base for anomaly explanation and solution retrieval.

faults.name: Loss of Signal (LOS) / Complete Communications Blackout
faults.telemetry_signature: Abrupt cessation of downlink telemetry (data channel goes flat, stale, or missing entirely) - typically a sharp point anomaly at onset followed by a sustained contextual gap.
likely_causes: Ground antenna failure or scheduling conflict
Environmental radio-frequency interference
Spacecraft attitude pointing error (antenna no longer aimed at Earth)
Onboard receiver/transmitter hardware failure or accidental power-off via an erroneous command sequence
recommended_actions: Initiate automated 'Command Loss Response' - spacecraft attempts to re-establish uplink autonomously
Check attitude/pointing telemetry (if available) to rule out an antenna pointing error before assuming hardware failure
Escalate to ground antenna operations to rule out ground-station-side causes

real_world_example.summary: Loss of uplink signal can stem from ground antenna failures, environmental interference, spacecraft hardware failures, erroneous attitude/pointing, RF interference, or an uplinked sequence error (e.g. a radio device accidentally turned off). Standard fault protection responds with an autonomous, endless-loop 'Command Loss Response' until contact is re-established.
real_world_example.source: Fault Protection Techniques in JPL Spacecraft, P. Morgan

faults.name: Anomalous Downlink / Partial Signal Lock-Up
faults.telemetry_signature: Signal present but degraded - off-nominal carrier power (too low or too high) or partial lock (missing subcarrier, symbol, telemetry, or frame lock). Shows as a contextual anomaly rather than a total data gap.
likely_causes: Spacecraft not earth-pointed as expected (incomplete turn, attitude control fault, or fault-protection activation)
Ground station equipment malfunction or mishandling
Onboard flight software coding error affecting the downlink chain
Space environment effects on the RF link
recommended_actions: Follow a structured LOS/Anomalous Downlink contingency procedure with troubleshooting flowcharts
Check for a preceding attitude anomaly that may explain off-pointing
Differentiate ground-station-side vs spacecraft-side causes before committing to a fix

real_world_example.summary: Cassini's RF Subsystem used an 'LOS/Anomalous Downlink Contingency Plan' to diagnose off-nominal carrier power and partial lock-up conditions, with five candidate fault categories considered before determining the recovery action.

faults.name: Data/Memory Corruption in the Telemetry Data Chain
faults.telemetry_signature: Downlinked telemetry becomes unreadable or garbled rather than absent - a distinctive contextual anomaly pattern (data present but statistically nonsensical / inconsistent with the encoding scheme).
likely_causes: Memory corruption in the flight data subsystem responsible for packaging telemetry before transmission
Radiation-induced bit-flip errors (single-event upsets) in onboard memory
Aging hardware in a long-duration mission
recommended_actions: Request a full memory readout ('poke') to identify the extent and location of corruption
Reroute affected processes to a working memory sector if the system supports remapping
Cross-check the fraction of corrupted memory against known safe operating thresholds before further action

real_world_example.summary: In 2024 Voyager 1 began sending unreadable data, traced to its Flight Data Subsystem (FDS). A ground-commanded memory readout confirmed about 3% of FDS memory was corrupted, preventing normal operation until engineers relocated the affected code.

faults.name: Antenna Pointing / Mechanical Misalignment
faults.telemetry_signature: Gradually weakening signal strength correlated with attitude/pointing telemetry drift - a slow contextual anomaly rather than a sudden failure, often worsening over a tumble or slew event.
likely_causes: Antenna misalignment from a tumbling or off-nominal spacecraft attitude
Deployable antenna mechanism partial failure
Power supply disruption to pointing/gimbal mechanisms (e.g. tin-whisker-induced short circuits in older hardware)
recommended_actions: Cross-reference with attitude control telemetry to confirm a pointing-related cause
Command a re-acquisition slew once attitude is stabilized
If mechanical, assess whether a backup/omnidirectional antenna can restore minimal contact

real_world_example.summary: Common technical failures behind communications blackouts include antenna misalignment from tumbling spacecraft and power distribution short-circuits (e.g. tin-whisker growth), both of which can cause total or partial loss of communication capability.

faults.name: Transponder Gain Drift
faults.telemetry_signature: Downlink signal strength slowly declines while uplink command reception stays nominal - a slow contextual anomaly isolated to one direction of the RF chain.
likely_causes: Amplifier component aging within the transponder
Thermal-cycling-induced gain shift
Partial degradation of an RF connector or waveguide
recommended_actions: Trend downlink signal strength against thermal telemetry to check for a temperature correlation
Switch to a redundant transponder chain if available
Adjust ground station tracking margins if degradation is gradual and bounded

faults.name: Uplink Command Rejection / CRC Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Commands sent to the spacecraft are received but rejected due to checksum/CRC mismatch - shows as a point anomaly in command-acceptance telemetry rather than the RF signal itself.
likely_causes: Bit errors introduced during transmission (weak signal, interference)
Ground station encoding configuration mismatch
Onboard receiver hardware fault corrupting received data
recommended_actions: Re-send the command and check if the error is transient (weak-signal-related) vs persistent (hardware-related)
Verify ground station uplink configuration matches spacecraft expectations
Escalate to receiver hardware review if rejection rate stays elevated

faults.name: Downlink Bit Error Rate Increase
faults.telemetry_signature: Frame/packet error rate on the downlink rises without a corresponding drop in raw signal strength - a contextual anomaly distinct from a simple weak-signal condition.
likely_causes: Interference from another RF source
Onboard modulator/encoder fault
Ground station demodulator misconfiguration or fault
recommended_actions: Check for known interference sources during the affected pass
Compare error rate across multiple ground stations to isolate spacecraft-side vs ground-side cause
Review onboard encoder telemetry/status if available

faults.name: Solar Conjunction Blackout
faults.telemetry_signature: Complete, predictable loss of usable downlink for an extended period (days to weeks) coincident with the Sun passing between Earth and spacecraft - a known, schedulable contextual anomaly rather than an unexpected fault.
likely_causes: Sun's radio noise overwhelming the communication link during solar conjunction
Predictable orbital/planetary geometry, not a hardware failure
recommended_actions: Confirm the blackout aligns with the predicted conjunction window before treating it as a fault
Ensure onboard data buffering is sized to hold science/engineering data for the blackout duration
Resume normal operations monitoring once conjunction geometry clears

faults.name: Doppler Shift Tracking Error
faults.telemetry_signature: Signal lock is intermittently lost during high-relative-velocity passes - point anomalies clustered near closest-approach or high-rate orbital phases.
likely_causes: Ground station Doppler compensation model inaccuracy
Faster-than-expected relative velocity change (e.g. unplanned maneuver)
Receiver tracking loop bandwidth insufficient for the rate of change
recommended_actions: Verify the Doppler prediction model against actual orbital elements
Widen receiver tracking loop bandwidth if the platform supports it
Cross-check for a recent maneuver that wasn't reflected in the tracking model

faults.name: RF Power Amplifier Degradation
faults.telemetry_signature: Transmitted power output telemetry declines relative to commanded power setting - a slow contextual anomaly in the amplifier's own housekeeping telemetry, separate from received signal strength.
likely_causes: Amplifier component aging (common in traveling-wave-tube or solid-state amplifiers)
Thermal stress reducing amplifier efficiency over time
Power supply instability feeding the amplifier
recommended_actions: Cross-check amplifier power supply telemetry for a root cause before assuming the amplifier itself has failed
Switch to a redundant amplifier chain if available
Adjust link budget expectations if degradation is gradual and within acceptable margins

faults.name: Antenna Deployment Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Deployment status telemetry never confirms full deployment, or signal strength stays far below expected post-deployment levels - a point anomaly tied to a specific one-time deployment event.
likely_causes: Mechanical jamming of the deployment mechanism
Deployment actuator (motor/pyro) failure
Thermal binding preventing full mechanism travel
recommended_actions: Re-attempt the deployment command sequence if the mechanism supports retry
Thermally cycle the mechanism (if commandable) to relieve possible thermal binding
Fall back to a lower-gain/omnidirectional antenna for continued minimal communications if redeployment fails

faults.name: Frequency Synthesizer Drift
faults.telemetry_signature: Carrier frequency slowly drifts outside the expected tracking window - a slow contextual anomaly requiring ground station frequency search to reacquire lock.
likely_causes: Oscillator aging
Temperature-induced frequency drift in the synthesizer
Radiation-induced component parameter shift
recommended_actions: Widen ground station frequency search window to reacquire lock
Trend frequency drift against thermal telemetry for a temperature correlation
Update predicted frequency tables used for pass planning

faults.name: Multipath / Ground-Environment Interference
faults.telemetry_signature: Signal strength shows rapid, repeating fades correlated with antenna elevation angle rather than a steady decline - a contextual anomaly tied to ground station geometry.
likely_causes: Signal reflection off nearby structures or terrain at the ground station
Low elevation-angle passes increasing susceptibility to multipath
Atmospheric scintillation during specific weather conditions
recommended_actions: Cross-check against elevation angle and known local RF environment before assuming a spacecraft-side cause
Prefer higher-elevation passes for critical commanding when the issue recurs
Coordinate with ground station operations if the pattern is consistent

faults.name: Ground Station Handover Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Brief telemetry gap precisely at a scheduled transition between ground stations (e.g. DSN complex handover) - a short, predictable point anomaly rather than an onboard fault.
likely_causes: Timing mismatch between outgoing and incoming ground station acquisition
Incorrect handover scheduling parameters
Brief loss of predicted pointing geometry during transition
recommended_actions: Confirm the gap aligns exactly with the scheduled handover window before investigating further
Review handover timing margins with ground network operations
Treat as a scheduling/ops issue, not a spacecraft anomaly, unless the gap significantly exceeds the expected handover duration

faults.name: Onboard Telemetry Buffer Overflow
faults.telemetry_signature: Data gaps or dropped packets appear despite a nominal RF link - a contextual anomaly best diagnosed via onboard buffer-fill-level telemetry rather than the RF signal itself.
likely_causes: Downlink data rate insufficient for the rate of data generation
Extended period without a scheduled downlink pass
A stuck or slow downlink process failing to drain the buffer
recommended_actions: Check buffer fill-level trend to distinguish this from an RF link problem
Schedule an additional or longer downlink pass to relieve the backlog
Review onboard data generation rate against the current downlink schedule

faults.name: Command Sequence Timing Error
faults.telemetry_signature: A commanded action executes at the wrong time or out of expected sequence relative to other commands - a point anomaly visible in command-execution log telemetry.
likely_causes: Onboard clock drift affecting scheduled command execution
Incorrect time-tag on an uplinked command sequence
Command queue processing delay
recommended_actions: Cross-check onboard clock telemetry against ground reference time
Review the uplinked command sequence for a time-tagging error before re-sending
If clock drift is the cause, schedule a clock correction/sync command

faults.name: Encryption/Authentication Handshake Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Uplink commands are received at the RF level but rejected at the protocol/security layer - a point anomaly isolated to the authentication stage, distinct from a CRC/bit-error rejection.
likely_causes: Key/certificate synchronization mismatch between ground and spacecraft
Onboard security processing fault
Ground station using an outdated credential set
recommended_actions: Verify ground and spacecraft security credentials are in sync before re-attempting
Check for a recent key-rotation event that may not have propagated correctly
Escalate to security/crypto subsystem review if resync attempts fail

faults.name: Low-Gain / High-Gain Antenna Switchover Fault
faults.telemetry_signature: Signal strength drops sharply at a commanded antenna switch event and does not recover to the expected level for the newly selected antenna - a point anomaly tied to a specific switching command.
likely_causes: RF switch mechanism failing to fully transition
Incorrect antenna selected due to a commanding error
Degraded performance on the newly selected antenna itself
recommended_actions: Re-issue the antenna selection command and verify switch-status telemetry
Cross-check against known health of both antennas before assuming a switch mechanism fault
Revert to the previous antenna if the new one shows degraded performance

faults.name: Co-located RF Source Interference
faults.telemetry_signature: Intermittent signal degradation correlated with another onboard subsystem's transmitter/receiver activity - a contextual anomaly with a timing pattern matching another subsystem's duty cycle.
likely_causes: Insufficient RF isolation between co-located transmitters/receivers
Harmonic interference from another onboard RF source
Shared power bus noise coupling into the RF chain
recommended_actions: Correlate anomaly timing with other onboard RF-emitting subsystems' operating schedules
Adjust operational timing to avoid simultaneous use where possible
Escalate to RF/EMC engineering review if interference is structural rather than schedule-avoidable

faults.name: Telemetry Frame Synchronization Loss
faults.telemetry_signature: Ground receives RF signal at expected strength but cannot lock onto frame boundaries to decode telemetry - a point anomaly at the framing/protocol layer despite a healthy physical-layer signal.
likely_causes: Onboard frame sync pattern generator fault
Bit-rate mismatch between transmitted and expected data rate
Corrupted onboard telemetry formatting configuration
recommended_actions: Verify ground receiver is configured for the correct bit rate and frame format
Check onboard telemetry formatter status/configuration telemetry if available
Attempt a reconfiguration command to reset the onboard formatter
